title: access.api-keys
behavior: access.api-keys is the client credential list for this proxy, not an upstream provider key. A present v8 value, including an empty list, replaces a legacy root api-keys string list. A root api-keys mapping is the upstream provider groups and is not read as this list. Blank entries are dropped and duplicates are ignored. With no remaining keys the config-api-key provider is not registered and the public proxy routes accept requests without a credential. Otherwise the first configured match is taken from Authorization (a Bearer token, or the whole header when it is not Bearer), X-Goog-Api-Key, X-Api-Key, query key, then query auth_token. Missing credentials return 401 {"error":"Missing API key"}; a presented value that matches none returns 401 {"error":"Invalid API key"}. Realtime routes that use the realtime middleware wrap the same failures as error.type authentication_error and code invalid_api_key. On a normal start or TUI standalone, outside Home, login/import commands, and cloud deploy with a missing config file, the template values your-api-key-1, your-api-key-2, and your-api-key-3 enable example-key safe mode. Those proxy prefixes then return 403 unsafe_example_api_key with X-CPA-SAFE-MODE: example-api-key, and GET or HEAD / and /management.html show the warning page unless the query is safe-mode=configure.

title: Meta login

title: Vertex login
behavior: Vertex service-account import is started by --vertex-import. It stores the service account JSON as a vertex credential; it is not a browser OAuth login.

title: Xai login
behavior: xAI device-code login is started by --xai-login.

title: --antigravity-login
behavior: Login to Antigravity with a browser OAuth callback. The default local listener is port 51121 and the redirect path is /oauth-callback. --oauth-callback-port greater than 0 replaces the port. --no-browser prints the URL instead of opening a browser. The wait is 5 minutes. A port or authentication failure is logged and the command returns without the Claude/Codex exit code 13.

title: --claude-login
behavior: Login to Claude with a browser OAuth callback. The default local listener is port 54545. --oauth-callback-port greater than 0 replaces it. --no-browser prints the URL and SSH tunnel hint instead of opening a browser. The wait is 5 minutes. If the port is already in use the process exits with code 13.

title: --codex-device-login
behavior: Login to Codex with the device-code flow. The command prints the device URL https://auth.openai.com/codex/device and a device code, and opens that URL unless --no-browser is set. It does not listen on the OAuth callback port. The wait is 15 minutes.

title: --codex-login
behavior: Login to Codex with a browser OAuth callback. The default local listener is port 1455 and the redirect path is /auth/callback. --oauth-callback-port greater than 0 replaces the port. --no-browser prints the URL instead of opening a browser. The wait is 5 minutes. If the port is already in use the process exits with code 13.

title: --config
behavior: When Postgres, object storage, Git, and Home are not supplying config, --config selects the YAML file to load. An empty value loads config.yaml from the working directory. If Home already supplied the config, a non-empty --config is kept only as the downstream path and is not loaded again.

title: --devin-login
behavior: Login to Devin. Without --no-browser it binds a callback, by default an ephemeral port or --oauth-callback-port when greater than 0, at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback and opens the browser. The wait is 5 minutes. With --no-browser it prints the URL and requires a pasted authorization code or session token. A state mismatch fails the login.

title: --discover
behavior: --discover scans the LAN for AI gateways and CLIProxyAPI instances, prints the result, and exits without starting the proxy. --discover-json enters the same scan.

title: --config
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --config selects the YAML file whose discovery.interfaces include and exclude lists are read. An empty value uses config.yaml in the working directory. A missing or invalid file yields empty filters and does not fail the scan. This flag does not start the server and is not the top-level --config.

title: --discover-exclude
behavior: With --discover or --discover-json, --discover-exclude skips comma-separated interface names. Matching is case-insensitive, and a trailing * is a prefix. If either this flag or --discover-include is non-empty, both CLI lists replace the config-file filters.

title: --discover-include
behavior: With --discover or --discover-json, --discover-include scans only the named interfaces and overrides the default physical LAN name filter. Matching is case-insensitive, and a trailing * is a prefix. If either this flag or --discover-exclude is non-empty, both CLI lists replace the config-file filters.

title: --discover-json
behavior: --discover-json runs the LAN scan, writes a JSON array of gateways to stdout, and exits. The version banner stays off stdout. Scan errors are a JSON object with error and an empty gateways array, and the process exits 1.

title: --discover-service-type
behavior: With --discover or --discover-json, --discover-service-type sets the DNS-SD service type. An empty value uses _ai-gateway._tcp.

title: --discover-timeout
behavior: With --discover or --discover-json, --discover-timeout sets the scan timeout in seconds. Values of 0 or less are treated as 3 seconds, and values above 60 seconds are capped at 60 seconds.

title: --exclude
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --exclude skips comma-separated interface names. Matching is case-insensitive, and a trailing * is a prefix. If either --include or --exclude is non-empty, both CLI lists replace the config-file filters.

title: --home-disable-cluster-discovery
behavior: Disable Home CLUSTER NODES discovery and keep using the configured -home-jwt address

title: --home-jwt
behavior: Home control plane JWT for mTLS certificate bootstrap and connection

title: --include
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --include scans only the named interfaces and overrides the default physical LAN name filter. Matching is case-insensitive, and a trailing * is a prefix. If either --include or --exclude is non-empty, both CLI lists replace the config-file filters.

title: --json
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --json prints discovered gateways as a JSON array and suppresses the version banner. Errors are a JSON object with error and an empty gateways array, and the process exits 1.

title: --kimi-ai-login
behavior: Login to Kimi.ai with the OAuth device-code flow. The command prints the verification URL and user code and opens the URL unless --no-browser is set. The saved provider is kimi-ai. --oauth-callback-port is not used.

title: --kimi-login
behavior: Login to Kimi.com with the OAuth device-code flow. The command prints the verification URL and user code and opens the URL unless --no-browser is set. The saved provider is kimi. --oauth-callback-port is not used.

title: --local-model
behavior: --local-model uses embedded model catalogs where models.catalog, models.codex-catalog, or models.devin-catalog is empty. A non-empty catalog value still wins for that catalog. It is applied for a normal server start and for TUI standalone, not for TUI client-only mode.

title: --management-base-url
behavior: Base URL of remote management API for TUI client mode (e.g. https://proxy.example.com)

title: --meta-login
behavior: Login to Meta Muse with the OAuth device-code flow. The command prints the verification URL and user code and opens the URL unless --no-browser is set. --oauth-callback-port is not used.

title: --no-browser
behavior: --no-browser stops OAuth login from opening a browser and prints the authorization URL instead. Devin login in this mode prints the authorization URL and asks for a pasted authorization code or session token. The CLI installs a default interactive prompt when the caller did not supply one.

title: --oauth-callback-port
behavior: --oauth-callback-port overrides the local OAuth callback port for login commands and --siwc-bind when the value is greater than 0. The default 0 keeps each provider's own port. Devin's own default is an ephemeral port.

title: --password
behavior: --password sets the local management password and is omitted from the usage text. Only a normal server start with a non-empty value registers GET /keep-alive. That endpoint returns 401 invalid password when the password is missing or wrong. The idle timer starts when the endpoint is enabled, so the process exits after 10 seconds with no successful call, and also 10 seconds after the last successful call. TUI standalone uses the background service start, which does not register the endpoint and does not shut down on that timer, even when the flag is non-empty or a password was generated. Management requests still require a configured management secret or MANAGEMENT_PASSWORD before this password can be accepted, and only from localhost. An empty value sets no local password on a normal start; TUI standalone generates one only when this flag is empty.

title: --service-type
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --service-type sets the DNS-SD service type. An empty value uses _ai-gateway._tcp.

title: --siwc-bind
behavior: --siwc-bind names an existing Codex credential file, runs Sign in with ChatGPT, writes the SIWC section and use_siwc=true, and does not start the proxy. The value must be an absolute path or a bare filename inside the configured auth directory. --no-browser and --oauth-callback-port apply. A callback port already in use makes the process exit with an error.

title: --standalone
behavior: In TUI mode, start an embedded local server

title: --timeout
behavior: On the discover subcommand, --timeout sets the scan timeout in seconds. Values of 0 or less are treated as 3 seconds, and values above 60 seconds are capped at 60 seconds.

title: --tui
behavior: Start with terminal management UI

title: --vertex-import
behavior: Import a Google Cloud service account JSON file as a vertex credential. The path is required. --vertex-import-prefix, when set, must be one path segment without a slash. The saved location is us-central1. Missing project_id, unreadable files, and invalid JSON are logged and the command returns. A successful import prints Vertex credentials imported.

title: --vertex-import-prefix
behavior: --vertex-import-prefix sets one path segment used to namespace Vertex model names and the saved credential filename when --vertex-import runs. An empty value imports without a prefix. A value that still contains / after trimming slashes is rejected and nothing is saved. The flag alone does not import a key.

title: --xai-login
behavior: Login to xAI with the OAuth device-code flow. The command prints the verification URL and user code returned by xAI and opens the URL unless --no-browser is set. It waits until xAI reports expiry. --oauth-callback-port is not used by this flow.

title: credentials.concurrency.busy-retry-max
behavior: Upper wait before retrying a busy credential. An absent zero becomes 1s. It must be a positive whole number of milliseconds and must not be less than busy-retry-min.

title: credentials.concurrency.busy-retry-min
behavior: Lower wait before retrying a busy credential. An absent zero becomes 250ms. It must be a positive whole number of milliseconds and must not exceed busy-retry-max.

title: credentials.concurrency.cleanup-interval
behavior: Interval for credential-concurrency cleanup. An absent zero becomes 5s. The value must be positive.

title: credentials.concurrency.cpa-cancel-bound
behavior: Cancel bound for a CPA concurrency lease. An absent zero becomes 5s. It must be positive. Node heartbeat timeout plus reclaim-grace must exceed this value plus cpa-heartbeat-timeout.

title: credentials.concurrency.cpa-heartbeat-timeout
behavior: CPA heartbeat timeout for a concurrency lease. An absent zero becomes 3s. The value must be positive.

title: credentials.concurrency.lifecycle-config-revision
behavior: Home lifecycle configuration revision. An absent value stays 0 and is allowed. A present 0 or any negative value fails load: lifecycle configuration revision must be positive when present.

title: credentials.concurrency.max-limit
behavior: Maximum concurrent credential leases. An absent zero becomes 1000000. The value must be from 1 through 1000000.

title: credentials.concurrency.observation-barrier-revision
behavior: Observation barrier revision. It must not be negative. An absent value stays 0.

title: credentials.concurrency.reclaim-grace
behavior: Grace before reclaiming a concurrency lease. An absent zero becomes 5s. The value must be positive.

title: credentials.concurrency.release-flush-interval
behavior: Flush interval for concurrency releases. An absent zero becomes 250ms. It must be positive and must not exceed release-max-backoff.

title: credentials.concurrency.release-max-backoff
behavior: Maximum backoff for release flushes. An absent zero becomes 2s. It must be positive and must not be less than release-flush-interval.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-aggregate-groups
behavior: Maximum aggregate groups retained for in-flight observation. The loader fills 100000 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be from 1 through 100000.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-details
behavior: Maximum detail records. The loader fills 10000 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be from 0 through 10000.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-part-bytes
behavior: Maximum bytes in one in-flight snapshot part. The loader fills 262144 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be at least 1024.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-part-count
behavior: Maximum number of parts in one revision. The loader fills 64 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be from 1 through 64.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-revision-bytes
behavior: Maximum bytes in one in-flight revision. The loader fills 16777216 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be from max-part-bytes through 16777216 and must fit in max-part-count parts.

title: credentials.in-flight.max-string-bytes
behavior: Maximum bytes kept for one observed string. The loader fills 256 before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be from 1 through 256.

title: credentials.in-flight.snapshot-interval
behavior: Interval for in-flight credential snapshots. The loader fills 2s before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be a positive duration, and stale-after must be at least three times this interval.

title: credentials.in-flight.staging-retention
behavior: How long staged in-flight observation data is retained. The loader fills 1m before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be a positive duration.

title: credentials.in-flight.stale-after
behavior: Age after which an in-flight snapshot is stale. The loader fills 10s before YAML decode when the field is absent. It must be a positive duration at least three snapshot intervals.

title: requests.tls-handshake-timeout-seconds
behavior: TLSHandshakeTimeoutSeconds bounds upstream TLS handshakes made by the shared uTLS client, in seconds. It applies to both the Claude Code Anthropic transport and the Chrome ChatGPT/Codex transport; the standard fallback transport is unaffected. It starts after TCP or proxy connection establishment returns and does not bound dialing or proxy CONNECT. Those uTLS paths use custom TLS dialing, for which Go ignores http.Transport.TLSHandshakeTimeout, so a peer that accepts the connection but never answers the ClientHello would otherwise block the request indefinitely and request-retry could never engage. The bound applies only during the TLS handshake and is removed once it succeeds, so inference and long-running streams are unaffected. The default 0 disables the bound (previous behavior); negative values are treated as 0, and values beyond the representable duration range saturate.

An empty model becomes grok-imagine-video. xAI video models and sora-2 or sora-2- prefixed models are accepted; other models return 400 telling the caller to use sora-2. prompt is required. Empty seconds becomes 4 and is clamped to 1 through 15. Empty size becomes 720x1280, and size must be one of 720x1280, 1280x720, 1024x1792, or 1792x1024. title: GET /v1/live/:call_id

A non-upgrade returns 426 WebSocket upgrade required. A busy session returns 409, and a missing session returns 404, both as a string error. A principal mismatch returns 403 with code realtime_call_scope_mismatch.

title: GET /v1/models
behavior: GET /v1/models is behind client API-key authentication. A User-Agent containing grok-shell returns the Grok Shell catalog. The presence of query client_version returns the Codex client catalog, or the Home Codex client catalog when Home is enabled. Anthropic-Version, or a User-Agent prefix claude-cli, returns the Claude catalog. Otherwise the response is an OpenAI list containing id, object, created, and owned_by. Home uses the Home catalog; a missing control center returns 503 home control center unavailable, a fetch failure returns 502, and a Home authentication failure keeps that status with type authentication_error. Encoding the Codex client catalog failure returns 500.

title: GET /v1/models/*model

No match returns 404 with code model_not_found. A valid catalog with neither a data nor a models array is also that 404, not 502. 502 Invalid model catalog happens only when json.Unmarshal of the whole catalog fails.

title: GET /v1/realtime

A call_id query switches to the sideband relay. Otherwise a WebSocket upgrade is required and a missing model query uses gpt-realtime, which selects gpt-live-1-codex. A client-secret model mismatch returns 403 realtime_client_secret_scope_mismatch. A non-upgrade returns 426 websocket_upgrade_required.

title: GET /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id
behavior: GET /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id uses realtime authentication and relays the sideband WebSocket for that call id. The id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$. Non-upgrade, invalid id, busy, and missing-session errors are wrapped with code realtime_request_failed. A client-secret or principal mismatch returns 403.

title: GET /v1/realtime/translations
behavior: GET /v1/realtime/translations uses realtime authentication and returns 501. The message is Realtime translation sessions are not supported by the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth upstream, with code realtime_capability_not_supported.

title: GET /v1/responses
behavior: GET /v1/responses is behind client API-key authentication and upgrades the connection to a WebSocket. The upgrader allows any Origin. JSON text messages of type response.create, response.append, and response.interrupt are accepted; response.interrupt is forwarded to the current upstream socket and does not start a new turn. If the upstream requires HTTP replay, the socket closes with code 1012 and reason upstream requires HTTP replay. A failed upgrade does not start a session.

title: GET /v1/videos/:request_id
behavior: GET /v1/videos/:request_id is behind client API-key authentication. The path parameter is request_id, with video_id as a fallback. An empty id returns 400 request_id is required. Retrieval uses the xAI native video handler and the default routing model grok-imagine-video.

title: POST /v1/alpha/search
behavior: POST /v1/alpha/search is behind client API-key authentication and reads at most 16 MiB. Optional JSON id becomes the selection X-Session-ID, and model selects the Codex credential. prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention are removed from a JSON object before forwarding. An API-key Codex credential must have a base URL and is called at that URL plus /alpha/search; a missing base URL returns 503 Codex Alpha Search API key base URL unavailable. A non-codex model-router target is rejected. The upstream status, body, and Content-Type are written back. Auth manager or credential unavailability returns 503.

title: POST /v1/audio/speech
behavior: POST /v1/audio/speech is behind client API-key authentication. The body is limited to 1 MiB. Empty, tts-1, tts-1-hd, gpt-4o-mini-tts, and grok-tts route as grok-tts; grok-voice-tts-1.0 stays itself. Prefixes xai/, x-ai/, and grok/ and a trailing parenthetical suffix are removed before that check. input or else text is required and limited to 60000 runes. The default voice is eve, language defaults to auto, and response_format defaults to mp3 with wav and pcm also accepted.

title: POST /v1/chat/completions
behavior: POST /v1/chat/completions is behind client API-key authentication. JSON boolean stream true returns SSE; any other stream value returns one JSON body. A body that has no messages but has input or instructions is converted from Responses shape into Chat Completions before execution. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error and a message starting Invalid request:.

title: POST /v1/completions
behavior: POST /v1/completions is behind client API-key authentication. JSON boolean stream true returns SSE; otherwise the response object is text_completion. An empty prompt is sent as the user text Complete this:. Existing model, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, stop, stream, logprobs, top_logprobs, and echo are copied. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error.

title: POST /v1/images/edits
behavior: POST /v1/images/edits is behind client API-key authentication. When disable-image-generation is true it returns 404 with an empty body. application/json uses the JSON editor; multipart/form-data or an empty Content-Type uses the form editor; any other type returns 400 unsupported Content-Type. prompt is required. The form image comes from image[] or image. An empty model becomes gpt-image-2.

title: POST /v1/images/generations
behavior: POST /v1/images/generations is behind client API-key authentication. When disable-image-generation is true it returns 404 with an empty body. The body must be valid JSON, prompt is required, an empty model becomes gpt-image-2, and an empty response_format becomes b64_json. Only a case-insensitive url stays url. JSON boolean stream true returns SSE. Unsupported models return 400 listing the accepted image model names.

title: POST /v1/live
behavior: POST /v1/live is inside the /v1 client API-key group and forwards a Codex realtime call bootstrap. The body limit is 16 MiB. A missing model uses gpt-live-1-codex. JSON, multipart, or an empty content type is accepted. Names gpt-realtime, gpt-realtime- prefixes, and names containing realtime-preview select gpt-live-1-codex. Errors from this path use {"error":"message"}. Oversized bodies return 413 Codex live request body too large. Missing auth returns 503.

title: POST /v1/messages
behavior: POST /v1/messages is behind client API-key authentication. A missing stream or JSON boolean false returns one JSON body; any other present stream value returns SSE. model selects execution. A claude-fable-5-dd- reversed model id is restored before routing. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error. Execution errors use a Claude error object; a direct upstream body recognized as thread_not_found is rewritten with error.details.error_code thread_not_found. A non-streaming body that starts with the gzip magic number is decompressed before it is written.

title: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens
behavior: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens is behind client API-key authentication and always writes JSON. It uses the model field and restores a claude-fable-5-dd- reversed model id before execution. Content-Type is set to application/json first. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error.

title: POST /v1/realtime
behavior: POST /v1/realtime uses realtime authentication and calls the same call-bootstrap handler as POST /v1/live. Because the path is under /v1/realtime, handler errors are wrapped as an error object with code realtime_request_failed. The body limit remains 16 MiB and the default model remains gpt-live-1-codex.

title: POST /v1/realtime/calls
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/calls uses realtime authentication and calls the same call-bootstrap handler as POST /v1/live. Handler errors on this path are wrapped with code realtime_request_failed.

title: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/accept
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/accept uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and returns 501 Realtime SIP accept are not supported by the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth upstream, with code realtime_capability_not_supported.

title: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/hangup
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/hangup uses standard realtime client API-key authentication. The call id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$, a missing local call returns 404 realtime_call_not_found, and a principal mismatch returns 403 realtime_call_scope_mismatch. A known call is hung up with its pinned Codex OAuth credential and the upstream status and body are written back.

title: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/refer
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/refer uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and returns 501 Realtime SIP refer are not supported by the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth upstream, with code realtime_capability_not_supported.

title: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/reject
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/calls/:call_id/reject uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and returns 501 Realtime SIP reject are not supported by the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth upstream, with code realtime_capability_not_supported.

title: POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and does not accept an ek_ secret as the caller credential. An empty body is allowed. The default session is type realtime and model gpt-realtime. expires_after.anchor must be created_at when set, and seconds must be from 10 to 7200; omission lasts 10 minutes. The value starts with ek_. The response is value, expires_at, and session with Cache-Control no-store. Capacity is 1024 entries and 64 per issuer, returning 429 with Retry-After 1. The body limit is 64 KiB.

title: POST /v1/realtime/sessions
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/sessions is the legacy client-secret endpoint. It uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and treats the whole body as the session object. The success body adds client_secret.value and client_secret.expires_at to the realtime.session object. Lifetime and capacity rules match POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets.

title: POST /v1/realtime/transcription_sessions
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/transcription_sessions uses standard realtime client API-key authentication and returns 501. The message is Realtime transcription-only sessions are not supported by the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth upstream, with type not_supported_error and code realtime_capability_not_supported.

title: POST /v1/realtime/translations
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/translations uses realtime authentication and returns the same 501 translation capability error as GET /v1/realtime/translations.

title: POST /v1/realtime/translations/client_secrets
behavior: POST /v1/realtime/translations/client_secrets uses standard realtime client API-key authentication, not the ek_ client-secret authenticator, and returns the same 501 translation capability error.

title: POST /v1/responses
behavior: POST /v1/responses is behind client API-key authentication. JSON boolean stream true returns SSE; otherwise one JSON body is returned. model selects execution. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error. Missing a stream flusher returns 500.

title: POST /v1/responses/compact
behavior: POST /v1/responses/compact is behind client API-key authentication and is not streamable. JSON boolean stream true returns 400 Streaming not supported for compact responses. A stream field that exists but is not that boolean is deleted before non-streaming execution. A body read failure returns its status, or 400, with type invalid_request_error.

title: POST /v1/tts
behavior: POST /v1/tts is behind client API-key authentication and calls the same handler as POST /v1/audio/speech. An unsupported model still reports that it is not supported on /v1/audio/speech and tells the caller to use grok-tts.

title: POST /v1/videos
behavior: POST /v1/videos is behind client API-key authentication and calls the xAI native video handler. An empty model becomes grok-imagine-video. Only xAI video models are accepted. grok-imagine-video-1.5-preview is canonicalized to grok-imagine-video-1.5 before execution. Other models return 400 listing the native video paths and grok-imagine-video.

title: POST /v1/videos/edits
behavior: POST /v1/videos/edits is behind client API-key authentication and calls the same xAI native video handler as POST /v1/videos, with this path.

title: POST /v1/videos/extensions
behavior: POST /v1/videos/extensions is behind client API-key authentication and calls the same xAI native video handler as POST /v1/videos, with this path.

title: POST /v1/videos/generations
behavior: POST /v1/videos/generations is behind client API-key authentication and calls the same xAI native video handler as POST /v1/videos.

title: GET /v1beta/models
behavior: GET /v1beta/models is behind client API-key authentication and returns {"models":[...]}. Names gain a models/ prefix when missing, empty displayName and description are filled from the name, and a missing supportedGenerationMethods becomes ["generateContent"]. Home uses the Home Gemini catalog; a missing control center returns 503 home control center unavailable and a fetch failure returns 502.

title: GET /v1beta/models/*action
behavior: GET /v1beta/models/*action is behind client API-key authentication. The action with its leading slash removed matches a model name with or without the models/ prefix, and a hit is returned with that prefix. No match returns 404 Not Found with type not_found. An unbindable path returns 400. Home looks up the Home catalog with the same not-found body.

title: POST /v1beta/interactions
behavior: POST /v1beta/interactions is behind client API-key authentication. The JSON body must contain exactly one of model or agent. stream defaults to false and must be a boolean when present. A models/ prefix is removed from model before execution. A non-empty agent forces the Interactions provider and selects credentials with gemini-2.5-flash. stream true returns SSE. Invalid JSON, the model/agent rule, and a non-boolean stream return 400. Missing a flusher returns 500 Streaming not supported.

title: POST /v1beta/models/*action
behavior: POST /v1beta/models/*action is behind client API-key authentication. The path after the leading slash must be model:method. generateContent, streamGenerateContent, and countTokens are handled; any other method writes no response. A path that is not exactly those two segments returns 404 with the path plus not found. streamGenerateContent uses SSE unless alt or $alt is present and not sse, in which case raw chunks are written. Missing a flusher returns 500 Streaming not supported. A body read failure returns its status, or 400.

title: routing.cooldown.disable-cooling
behavior: DisableCooling disables auth/model cooldown scheduling when true unless a credential or provider overrides it.

title: routing.cooldown.save-cooldown-status
behavior: SaveCooldownStatus persists runtime cooldown status next to auth files when true.

title: routing.cooldown.transient-error-cooldown-seconds
behavior: TransientErrorCooldownSeconds controls cooldowns for transient upstream errors (408/500/502/503/504/520-526). 0 keeps the legacy default cooldown. Negative values disable these cooldowns.

title: routing.force-model-prefix
behavior: ForceModelPrefix requires explicit model prefixes (e.g., "teamA/gemini-3-pro-preview") to target prefixed credentials. When false, unprefixed model requests may use prefixed credentials as well.

title: routing.retry.max-retry-credentials
behavior: MaxRetryCredentials defines the maximum number of different credentials to try in each credential retry round. Set to 0 or a negative value to keep trying all available credentials (legacy behavior).

title: routing.retry.max-retry-interval
behavior: MaxRetryInterval defines the maximum positive cooldown wait, in seconds, allowed before starting another credential retry round. A non-positive value forbids positive cooldown waits; it does not disable same-round credential failover or immediate additional rounds allowed by RequestRetry.

title: routing.retry.request-retry
behavior: RequestRetry defines the number of additional credential retry rounds after the first round has exhausted its eligible credentials.

title: routing.session-affinity-rebind-on
behavior: SessionAffinityRebindOn controls which credential failures rebind an established session to the failover credential. Supported values: - "any" (default): any credential-attributed failure unbinds and rebinds on failover. - "quota": transient errors (408, 5xx, empty stream, buffer limit) fail over for that request only while keeping the session bound to its original credential; quota and auth errors (429, 401/402/403, 404/model support, invalid_grant) rebind as normal. Ignored when SessionAffinity is false.
defaults: Supported values: - "any" (default): any credential-attributed failure unbinds and rebinds on failover.

title: routing.session-affinity-subagents
behavior: SessionAffinitySubagents controls whether subagents (child sessions with parent references) inherit and bind to the parent's upstream credential across all providers (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini), maximizing prompt and KV cache reuse. When false, subagents are distributed across the credential pool via the fallback selector. Default: true. Ignored when SessionAffinity is false.

title: routing.session-affinity-ttl
behavior: SessionAffinityTTL specifies how long session-to-auth bindings are retained. Default: 1h. Accepts duration strings like "30m", "1h", "2h30m".

title: routing.session-affinity
behavior: SessionAffinity enables universal session-sticky routing for all clients. Explicit Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and pi session headers are preferred, followed by prompt_cache_key, Responses conversation IDs, legacy body IDs, execution or derived session identity, and the existing message-content hash fallback. Automatic failover is always enabled when bound auth becomes unavailable.

title: routing.strategy
behavior: Strategy selects the credential selection strategy. Supported values: "round-robin" (default), "weighted-round-robin", "fill-first".

title: server.commercial-mode
behavior: CommercialMode disables high-overhead request logging and HTTP middleware features to minimize per-request memory usage.

title: server.discovery.advertise-management
behavior: AdvertiseManagement explicitly controls whether management endpoints are exposed (default: false).
defaults: AdvertiseManagement explicitly controls whether management endpoints are exposed (default: false).

title: server.discovery.auth-required
behavior: AuthRequired indicates whether authentication is required for client calls (default: true).
defaults: AuthRequired indicates whether authentication is required for client calls (default: true).

title: server.discovery.enabled
behavior: Enabled toggles mDNS service advertising on the local network (default: false).
defaults: Enabled toggles mDNS service advertising on the local network (default: false).

title: server.discovery.interfaces.exclude
behavior: YAML server.discovery.interfaces.exclude

title: server.discovery.interfaces.include
behavior: YAML server.discovery.interfaces.include

title: server.discovery.service-name
behavior: ServiceName is the optional custom instance name. When empty, defaults to CPA-<ShortID>.

title: server.discovery.service-type
behavior: ServiceType is the DNS-SD service type (default: _ai-gateway._tcp).
defaults: ServiceType is the DNS-SD service type (default: _ai-gateway._tcp).

title: server.discovery.subtypes
behavior: Subtypes specifies DNS-SD API protocol subtypes to advertise (e.g. _responses, _messages, _generate-content).

title: server.github-token
behavior: GitHubToken is the global token for GitHub requests, taking precedence over GITHUB_TOKEN.

title: server.host
behavior: Host is the network host/interface on which the API server will bind. Default is empty ("") to bind all interfaces (IPv4 + IPv6). Use "127.0.0.1" or "localhost" for local-only access.
defaults: Default is empty ("") to bind all interfaces (IPv4 + IPv6).

title: server.max-request-body-bytes
behavior: MaxRequestBodyBytes limits the size (in bytes) of incoming HTTP request bodies. Values <= 0 disable the limit (default).

title: server.port
behavior: Port is the network port on which the API server will listen.

title: server.tls.cert
behavior: Cert is the path to the TLS certificate file.

title: server.tls.enable
behavior: Enable toggles HTTPS server mode.

title: server.tls.key
behavior: Key is the path to the TLS private key file.

title: server.trusted-proxies
behavior: TrustedProxies lists the IPs or CIDRs allowed to provide forwarded client IP headers. The server applies this list at startup; changing it requires a restart.

title: upstream.claude.disable-claude-cloak-mode
behavior: DisableClaudeCloakMode globally disables Claude request cloaking when true. Cloaking disguises requests as the official Claude Code CLI and replaces the system prompt. When true, every Claude credential defaults to no cloaking ("never"); a specific credential can still re-enable or override it via its own cloak settings (the per claude-api-key "cloak" block, or a "cloak_mode" value in the auth/OAuth token file). Default false preserves the per-client "auto" behavior.
defaults: When true, every Claude credential defaults to no cloaking ("never"); a specific credential can still re-enable or override it via its own cloak settings (the per claude-api-key "cloak" block, or a "cloak_mode" value in the auth/OAuth token file).

title: upstream.claude.disable-cloaking-model-list
behavior: DisableCloakingModelList disables model ID cloaking in Anthropic model list responses.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.anthropic-beta-append
behavior: Exact Anthropic-Beta names appended when not already present. Strip runs first. Nil means no additions.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.anthropic-beta-strip
behavior: Exact Anthropic-Beta names removed from the final set, preserving order. Empty names and duplicates are dropped. Nil means no removals.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.arch
behavior: Arch value used when stabilize-device-profile pins the device profile. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.client-request-id
behavior: Controls x-client-request-id. Empty and on synthesize a UUID; passthrough forwards only the caller value; off sends nothing. Any other value is warned and reset to empty, which means on.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.inject-diagnostics
behavior: Nil keeps diagnostics injection for Claude Code CLI profiles, including real Claude OAuth. Explicit false stops injecting the diagnostics field and the cache-diagnosis beta.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.os
behavior: OS value used when stabilize-device-profile pins the device profile. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.package-version
behavior: Fallback Claude Code package version. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.runtime-version
behavior: Fallback Claude Code runtime version. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.stabilize-device-profile
behavior: When true, OS and arch are pinned and cached profiles stay on the configured software baseline. Nil or false does not pin them.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.timeout
behavior: Fallback timeout string for the Claude CLI fingerprint. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.timezone
behavior: Fallback IANA timezone for a cloaked currentDate. A credential JSON timezone takes priority. Empty leaves the field unset.

title: upstream.claude.header-defaults.user-agent
behavior: Fallback Claude Code user-agent baseline. Empty leaves the field unset. Verified native clients keep their shape only when their versions match this baseline.

title: upstream.claude.model-level-cooling
behavior: ModelLevelCooling scopes Claude quota cooldowns to the requested model rather than cooling down the entire credential across all sibling models.

title: upstream.claude.session-date-pin-days
behavior: SessionDatePinDays retains the cloaked currentDate pin per session for this many days, independently of continuity expiry and credential switches. A nil value (unset) defaults to 7 days; an explicit 0 keeps the continuity-scoped pin (1h lifetime).
defaults: A nil value (unset) defaults to 7 days; an explicit 0 keeps the continuity-scoped pin (1h lifetime).

title: upstream.claude.tool-search
behavior: ToolSearch enables Codex client tool_search on Claude Responses routes: Anthropic native tool search where the credential supports it, a pre-tool_search translation elsewhere, and per-credential search advertising in the Codex catalog. Default false keeps the translation that predates tool_search support.
defaults: Default false keeps the translation that predates tool_search support.

title: upstream.codex.disable-codex-cloaking
behavior: DisableCodexCloaking disables forcing the official Codex identity headers on HTTP/SSE and WebSocket requests.

title: upstream.codex.model-level-cooling
behavior: ModelLevelCooling scopes Codex usage_limit_reached quota cooldowns to the requested model rather than cooling down the entire credential across all sibling models.

title: upstream.codex.orphan-delegation-compatibility
behavior: OrphanDelegationCompatibility enables opt-in compatibility for orphan Codex delegation outputs.

title: upstream.codex.response-steering
behavior: ResponseSteering enables full-duplex Codex WebSockets, bound to one upstream model/account/socket for their entire lifetime. Default is false.

title: upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-buffering
behavior: StreamBootstrapBuffering holds back the frames that arrive before generation starts, none of which the client has seen anything from - the handshake (response.created, response.in_progress, the websocket metadata frames), keepalive heartbeats, and the *.added announcements of an item or part that is still empty - until the first generated event arrives. The upstream delivers server_is_overloaded rejections inside an HTTP 200 stream right after those frames instead of returning 503 on the wire, so buffering them keeps the downstream response headers uncommitted long enough to retry on another credential. Trade-off: the response headers are delayed until the upstream starts generating, which on a slow reasoning turn now means several heartbeat intervals rather than one, and can trip client or reverse-proxy read timeouts. The hold is bounded by a frame and a byte budget, not by wall-clock time, and neither budget is advanced by a websocket peer that sends only control frames or by an upstream that never terminates an SSE line. Only overload and rate-limit rejections fail over deliberately. A stream that ends while the bootstrap is still holding ends the attempt rather than reaching the client, and what follows is pre-existing but now far more likely, since the hold can span the whole reasoning phase instead of ending at the first keepalive: a clean end with no terminal event is request-scoped on SSE and stops there, while a websocket close or a transport error on either transport is not, so the request may be retried on another credential. Default is false.

title: upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-timeout
behavior: StreamBootstrapTimeout specifies an optional maximum duration to hold back uncommitted response headers during bootstrap buffering before releasing the stream to the client. Defaults to "0" (unlimited time, relying purely on the 48-frame and 1MB byte bounds). When set (e.g. "20s"), the stream is released once the time ceiling is reached, avoiding reverse-proxy timeouts (e.g. Nginx 60s proxy_read_timeout).
defaults: Defaults to "0" (unlimited time, relying purely on the 48-frame and 1MB byte bounds).

title: upstream.xai.inject-x-search
behavior: InjectXSearch injects xAI's native x_search tool when the request does not declare it.
